subject: Staged cutover: AtlasWorks capacity validation & sanity run
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft validation items and target windows for Dedicated cutover

Samir —

Thanks for the call today. Per our discussion, I put together a short checklist for the hosted->dedicated migration validation that we think will give AtlasWorks confidence before the cutover. Can you confirm whether the preferred maintenance window of Sep 21–22 (overnight UTC) still works for your infra team? If so, we’ll schedule a staged run in your staging VPC then a dry-run in production the following night.

High level validation steps (attached: AtlasWorks_MAT_reqs.xlsx):
- Capacity smoke: run 60-min steady-state at expected 75% p95 QPS
- Latency SLO checks: p50/p95/p99 token generation vs hosted baseline
- Cache warmup: KV cache priming and prefix hit rate verification
- Failover: simulate node replacement and verify graceful fallback to smaller variant
- Cost delta sanity: compare per-token compute vs hosted baseline (rough)

Next steps for us: Vivek and Marissa will produce an execution runbook and load scripts. Stephanie — can you confirm who on AtlasWorks procurement should be looped for formal approvals?

Thanks,
Ben
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 14:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft validation items and target windows for Dedicated cutover — sizing & load plan

Stephanie / team —

Attached are the artifacts and a short summary for AtlasWorks. High level conclusions up front:
- Baseline: AtlasWorks manifests show peak sustained concurrency equivalent to ~220 concurrent prompt sessions (avg 1.8 requests/min each) with median sequence lengths around 320 tokens.
- Recommended slice for staging: 4xA100-80GB (reserved) for the staged smoke; this gives ~3.2M token/sec aggregate in our microbench. For production dry-run, plan for 8xA100-80GB (or 12x if we include a 50% safety margin for unknown spikes).
- Expected P95 generation latency delta vs hosted: +12–18ms under identical batching; p99 tail depends on queueing during peak and should be tracked live.
- KV cache warmup: recommend prioritized prefix replay for first 30 minutes; expect hit rate to stabilize >85% by minute 20 during steady-state if we pre-seed with top 20k prefixes.
- Rollback criteria (short):
  * If p95 generation latency > 2x hosted baseline for >10 consecutive minutes OR error rate increases >1.5x, initiate rollback to hosted routing (automated fallback we tested) and notify on-call.

Attachments (stubs): load-scripts.tar.gz (contains k6 scripts + model priming), model_kv_cache_report.pdf (small report from our staging sim).

I’ll upload the full runbook to the Drive link and add a short run checklist for the on-call. If we target 21/22 as planned, we should rehearse a dry run on the 20th internally (30–60 minute smoke).

Vivek
Sr Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

Subject: Confirming staging window & providing cutover runbook link

Samir / Procurement —

Confirming: we have scheduled the internal dry-run (Redwood-only) rehearsals for Sep 20 20:00–21:00 PDT and the AtlasWorks staging smoke on Sep 21 20:00–23:00 PDT. Production dry-run remains Sep 22 22:00–01:00 PDT.

Runbook and artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2AtlasWorksCutover (contains the cutover-runbook.md and the load artifacts). DocuSign link for the dedicated addendum: https://docusign.com/link/ATX-DW-4821 (procurement — please complete by EOD 21 Sep).

Quick checklist for your ops team at start of staging smoke:
- Confirm monitoring dashboards visible to AtlasWorks (token rates, GPU utilization, KV hit rate)
- Run primer: run load-scripts/scripts/primer_kv_replay.sh for 20 minutes
- Start steady-state: start k6-stable.js at target concurrency for 60 minutes
- Checkpoints at T+15, T+30, T+60 minutes and report p50/p95/p99
- If rollback criteria met, toggle routing to hosted (we’ll coordinate) and open incident bridge.

If all good, we’ll run the production dry-run on the 22nd with the same checklist plus a sustainability test for 3 hours at 60% of expected peak.

Ben
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
